label: WRONG
reason: Router files (_app.ts, tags.ts, bank-accounts.ts) export routers built with createTRPCRouter; the outliers in init.ts are infrastructure (caller factory, procedure builders) that are not routers, so a new procedure builder or middleware export would be wrongly flagged.

label: ACCEPT
reason: Members like isValidJSON, isZeroDecimalCurrency, getStartOfDayUTC annotate return types; the two outliers are ordinary exported functions with inferred returns (could easily be annotated) and biome.json enables no rule requiring it, so it is a choice. Hesitated with WRONG as a style nit.

label: WRONG
reason: Router exports (tagsRouter, bankAccountsRouter) follow *Router, but init.ts also exports procedure builders and the caller factory (publicProcedure, protectedProcedure, internalProcedure), which are not routers; a new procedure builder would be told to be named *Router. Example createTRPCRouter is itself the odd one.

reason: Most opened outliers (disconnectProviderSchema, exportToAccountingSchema, getAccountsSchema, createCheckoutSchema, getJobStatusSchema) literally call z.object() (imported from zod rather than @hono/zod-openapi), so the tool misread them; the rest are enums/arrays that legitimately are not objects.

label: ACCEPT
reason: All 39 processor classes extend BaseProcessor (directly or via abstract AccountingProcessorBase); the registry only requires a structural { handle } so a class without BaseProcessor compiles and silently loses its retry/logging/validation handling, so no tool catches it and it is worth flagging.
